messages:
elaine: Short priming + quant scan on 'harbor-8b' (fp16 vs int8 vs int6) across 800 mixed slices (chat, extraction, long summary). Handoff notes for GTN/product.

priya: Can you paste the high-level numbers we can show product?

elaine: Quick scorecard (800 samples):
```
metric | fp16 | int8 | int6
QA F1 | 0.885 | 0.876 | 0.848
EM    | 0.801 | 0.794 | 0.760
ROUGE | 0.421 | 0.414 | 0.392
Cost/1k tok | $0.40 | $0.28 | $0.20
lat p50 ms | 105 | 118 | 130
```
Notes: int8 gives ~30% cost reduction with small average quality dip (~1%). int6 pushes cost ~50% down but hits multi-step extraction and numeric-normalization slices. Long summaries (>900 tok) degrade more under low-precision quant.

tom: Routing recommendation for GTN? simple language pls.

elaine: Tiered suggestion:
- Exploratory endpoints -> int6 (economy)
- Default/product endpoints -> int8 (balanced)
- Critical extraction / longform -> fp16 (premium)
Fallback: shadow 1% of int6/int8 traffic to fp16; auto-fallback to fp16 when rolling EM delta > 2% over 30m.

priya: Any quick guardrails to include in GTN blurb?

elaine: Yes:
- Hourly adversarial probe (100 examples) covering: numeric extraction, unit conversions, long coref. Fail if EM drop >3%.
- Monitor p95 latency: if int8/int6 p95 > fp16 p95 by 30% and error rate rises, throttle to balanced/premium.
- Enable short-prefix caching for chat to reduce token spend and stabilize int8.

ops-bot: bench-bot: Canary scheduled: canary/3752468001-quant -> 1k requests over 1h; report will post to #eng-ml/bench-reports.

priya: I'll craft a one-slide summary: "~30% cost savings w/ int8 (avg quality drop ~1%), ~50% w/ int6 (avg drop ~3-4%); recommend tiered defaults + 1% shadowing + hourly adversarial checks"

elaine: Cool. I'll attach per-slice breakdown after canary completes.
